_source.description: Major global bismuth mining, smelting, and refining sites — produced from bismuth ores and as byproduct of tungsten, lead, and copper refining
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/); China Nonferrous Metal Mining Group (CNMC) publications; Hunan Nonferrous Metals Corp reports; Masan Resources (now Masan High-Tech Materials) annual reports (https://masanhightechmaterials.com/); Yunnan Tin Group corporate reports; Korea Zinc annual reports; Umicore annual reports; Teck Resources annual reports; Vinto smelter (COMIBOL Bolivia) data
_source.license: USGS: public domain; company data: fair use summary
_source.notes: Bismuth is produced both from primary bismuth ores (often associated with tungsten, tin, and molybdenum deposits) and as a byproduct of lead, copper, and tin smelting/refining. China dominates global production at ~80% (~16,000 of ~20,000 tonnes/year). Major uses: pharmaceuticals (bismuth subsalicylate — Pepto-Bismol), fire safety (fusible alloys for sprinkler systems), low-melting-point alloys (Wood's metal, Field's metal), cosmetics (bismuth oxychloride), and as lead-free substitute in machining alloys, solders, and ammunition. Designated a USGS critical mineral. Coordinates from USGS MRDS, company filings, and satellite verification. Chinese production data is aggregated from multiple provincial reports; individual facility capacities are estimates.

sites.name: Shizhuyuan Polymetallic Mine (Chenzhou)
sites.ownership: China Minmetals / Hunan Nonferrous Metals Corp (state-owned)
sites.notes: Chenzhou, Hunan Province. World's largest single bismuth-producing mine. Shizhuyuan is a massive polymetallic skarn deposit containing tungsten, bismuth, molybdenum, and tin. Bismuth occurs in bismuthinite and native bismuth associated with the tungsten-molybdenum orebody. One of the world's most important bismuth sources.

sites.name: Ganzhou Bismuth/Tungsten District (Jiangxi)
sites.ownership: Jiangxi Tungsten Holding Group (Jiangxi provincial state) and various private operators
sites.notes: Ganzhou, southern Jiangxi Province. Major tungsten-bismuth mining district with numerous mines in the Nanling Range. Bismuth recovered as byproduct of tungsten mining and processing. Region hosts some of China's largest tungsten reserves.

sites.name: Yunnan Tin Group (Gejiu Smelter)
sites.ownership: Yunnan Tin Group (SZE: 000960; Yunnan provincial state majority)
sites.notes: Gejiu, Yunnan Province (historic 'Tin Capital' of China). World's largest tin producer. Bismuth recovered as byproduct of tin smelting and refining from the Gejiu polymetallic tin deposits. Significant bismuth source due to high throughput volumes.

sites.name: Guangdong Rising Nonferrous (Shaoguan)
sites.notes: Guangdong Province. Diversified nonferrous metals group with lead-zinc and tungsten operations. Bismuth recovered as byproduct from lead smelting and tungsten processing. One of Guangdong's largest nonferrous metals enterprises.

sites.name: Hunan Nonferrous Zhuzhou Smelter
sites.ownership: China Minmetals / Hunan Nonferrous Metals Corp (state-owned)
sites.notes: Zhuzhou, Hunan Province. One of China's largest lead-zinc smelters. Bismuth recovered from lead refining (bismuth concentrates in lead bullion and is separated during electrolytic or pyrometallurgical refining). Significant Chinese bismuth source.

sites.name: Guizhou Polymetallic Mining District
sites.notes: Guiyang/central Guizhou Province. Multiple small-to-medium polymetallic mines producing bismuth as byproduct of lead-zinc mining. Guizhou hosts significant bismuth-bearing lead-zinc deposits in carbonate-hosted ore systems.

sites.name: Hunan Yongzhou Bismuth Mining District
sites.ownership: Mixed state and private mining enterprises
sites.notes: Yongzhou, southern Hunan Province. Part of the broader Nanling metallogenic belt. Multiple bismuth-tungsten deposits mined by regional operators. Bismuth occurs as bismuthinite in quartz-vein and skarn-type deposits.

sites.name: Nui Phao Polymetallic Mine
sites.ownership: Masan High-Tech Materials (HOSE; Masan Group majority; H.C. Starck JV)
sites.notes: Dai Tu District, Thai Nguyen Province, northern Vietnam. One of the world's largest tungsten mines outside China. Major bismuth producer — one of the top non-Chinese sources globally. Polymetallic skarn/greisen deposit. Bismuth produced as concentrate and refined bismuth metal. Capacity ~1,500 tpa bismuth metal.

sites.name: Mexico Lead-Zinc Smelters (various)
sites.notes: Monterrey/Torreon area, northeastern Mexico. Penoles operates major lead-zinc smelting and refining complexes. Bismuth recovered as byproduct of lead refining (Betts electrolytic process or Kroll-Betterton drossing). Mexico is a significant bismuth producer from lead refinery byproducts.

sites.name: Vinto Tin Smelter
sites.notes: Oruro, Bolivia. State-owned tin smelter (capacity ~15,000 tpa tin). Bismuth recovered as byproduct of tin smelting from Bolivian tin concentrates. Bolivia has historically been a notable bismuth producer from its polymetallic tin-bismuth ores.

sites.name: Mitsubishi Materials (Naoshima Refinery)
sites.notes: Naoshima Island, Kagawa Prefecture. Bismuth recovered from copper anode slimes during electrolytic copper refining. Mitsubishi Materials is Japan's primary bismuth refiner, producing high-purity bismuth metal (99.99%+) for pharmaceutical and electronic applications.

sites.name: Dowa Holdings (Akita Refinery)
sites.notes: Kosaka/Akita Prefecture, northern Honshu. Dowa's integrated smelting complex recovers bismuth from lead refining and complex recyclable materials. Also produces high-purity bismuth compounds for electronics and specialty chemical markets.

sites.name: Peru Lead Smelter Byproduct (La Oroya/Doe Run)
sites.ownership: Peruvian state administration (Doe Run Peru under restructuring)
sites.notes: La Oroya, Junin Region, central Peruvian Andes. Historic polymetallic smelter (operating since 1922). Bismuth recovered from lead refining circuit. Operations suspended/reduced due to environmental remediation requirements and financial restructuring of Doe Run Peru. When operational, significant South American bismuth source.

sites.name: Teck Trail Operations
sites.notes: Trail, British Columbia. One of the world's largest integrated zinc-lead smelters. Bismuth recovered from lead refining circuit as byproduct. Trail has produced bismuth for decades as part of its diversified metals recovery operations.

sites.name: Umicore Precious Metals Refining (Hoboken)
sites.notes: Hoboken, Antwerp. World-leading precious metals and specialty metals recycling refinery. Bismuth recovered from complex recyclable materials and copper/lead refining byproducts. Produces high-purity bismuth for pharmaceutical and specialty applications.

sites.name: Phu Kham Copper-Gold Mine (Laos)
sites.notes: Phu Bia Mining area, Xaisomboun Province, central Laos. Copper-gold mine with bismuth as minor byproduct in copper concentrate. Bismuth reports to concentrate and is recovered at destination smelters. MMG acquired PanAust in 2015.

sites.name: Korea Zinc (Onsan Refinery)
sites.notes: Onsan National Industrial Complex, Ulsan. World's largest zinc refinery. Bismuth recovered from lead refining circuit and zinc residue processing. Korea Zinc produces refined bismuth metal as part of its comprehensive metals recovery operations.

sites.name: Nyrstar Port Pirie Smelter
sites.notes: Port Pirie, South Australia. One of the world's largest primary lead smelters. Bismuth recovered from lead bullion refining (Betts electrolytic process). Port Pirie has produced bismuth since the early 20th century. TSP (Transformation of the Smelter Project) upgraded recovery circuits.

sites.name: Doe Run Herculaneum (USA — closed)
sites.notes: Herculaneum, Missouri. Last primary lead smelter in the US; closed December 2013 due to EPA air quality regulations. When operational, bismuth was recovered as byproduct of lead refining. US now has no primary bismuth production; all bismuth is imported or recovered from secondary sources. Included for historical and strategic context.

sites.name: Hindustan Zinc (Chanderiya Lead-Zinc Smelter)
sites.notes: Chanderiya, Chittorgarh District, Rajasthan. India's largest integrated zinc-lead smelter. Bismuth recovered from lead refining circuit as minor byproduct. Hindustan Zinc is the world's second-largest zinc producer.
